findings.title: Update check uses the org-aware wrapper, so edits to IDPs of a disabled organization never invalidate the login cache
findings.body:
`original` comes from `getById(...)` (line 91). That method returns `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(...)`, and its `isEnabled()` returns false whenever the IDP's organization is disabled or organizations are turned off for the realm (lines 436-443). `updated` is a plain model built by `RepresentationToModel.toModel` (IdentityProviderResource.java:191), so its `isEnabled()` is the raw flag.

The login query does not look at organization state. `getForLogin` filters only DB columns (enabled, linkOnly, hideOnLogin, BROKER_PUBLIC; IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:165-184). So the cached ORG_ONLY/ALL id lists still contain IDPs whose organization is disabled. The bean only re-checks `isEnabled()` (OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java:75,80).

Scenario: org X is disabled. An admin sets its public IDP to `hideOnLogin=true`, `linkOnly=true`, or makes it non-public. `original` fails the predicate because the wrapper says it is disabled. `updated` fails because it is now hidden. The first early return (line 405) fires and nothing is invalidated. When org X is enabled again, the stale cached id is resolved through `getById` and passes the bean's `isEnabled()` filter. The hidden or link-only IDP then shows on the login page, with no error.

Fix: evaluate the predicate on the unwrapped stored state, e.g. `idpDelegate.getById(model.getInternalId())`, as `remove()` already does with `idpDelegate.getByAlias`. Or invalidate unconditionally when the stored model's raw fields differ in any login-filter field.

findings.title: Cleanup removes a literal "alias" IDP, not the IDPs the test creates
findings.body: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` registers removal of an IDP named `alias`, which never exists. The 21 IDPs created here (`idp-alias-0..20`, also line 425) are never cleaned up by this hook. The pattern was copied from line 303. Use `get(idpRep.getAlias())`, captured in a local variable.

findings.title: No coverage for organization-link removal or org enable/disable against the login cache
findings.body: The test covers create, remove, plain updates and linking an IDP to an org. It does not cover `removeIdentityProvider` (unlink, which clears BROKER_PUBLIC; JpaOrganizationProvider.java:367-371). It also does not cover edits made while the organization is disabled, which is where the invalidation check above goes wrong.

contracts.action: Login IDP lists are cached per realm and fetch mode, keyed by organization id
contracts.before_after: Mirrors getByOrganization: on a miss it loads ids from the delegate and adds a revisioned query. If the search key is missing, it invalidates the object and re-adds it with the merged keys. Each id is resolved through getById, and if an IDP has vanished the query is invalidated and the delegate is used.
contracts.visible_effect: The resolved IDPs feed IdentityProviderBean/OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.searchForIdentityProviders, which render the login page buttons.
contracts.failure_mode: Correctness depends on invalidation in create/update/remove. The update check uses the org-aware wrapper, so edits made while an organization is disabled can leave stale ids (see finding).

contracts.action: Org link/unlink goes through identityProviders().update, which triggers login-cache invalidation
contracts.before_after: addIdentityProvider sets organizationId and calls update. removeIdentityProvider clears organizationId and BROKER_PUBLIC, then calls update. In both cases the orgId changes, so the cache is invalidated whenever either side qualifies for login.
contracts.visible_effect: The login page reflects linking or unlinking on the next render.

contracts.action: getLoginPredicate now requires BROKER_PUBLIC for org-linked IDPs
contracts.equivalent_path: Default getForLogin search options (BROKER_PUBLIC=true for org IDPs) and OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.isPublicOrganizationBroker
contracts.before_after: The predicate is also used by IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so federated-identity IDP lists now drop non-public org IDPs as well. The org-aware bean already applied that filter.
contracts.visible_effect: Users with a federated link to a non-public org IDP no longer see it in the base bean's list.

summary: The PR caches the login IDP lists in Infinispan, keyed by realm and fetch mode, and invalidates them on create, remove and updates that change login eligibility. One fix: `update()` checks eligibility on the org-aware wrapper from `getById`, whose `isEnabled()` is false while the organization is disabled. Edits made in that state (hide on login, link-only, non-public) skip invalidation, and the hidden IDP shows on the login page once the organization is enabled again. Two test notes: the new test's cleanup hooks remove a literal "alias" IDP instead of the ones it creates, and unlinking an IDP from an org and edits made while the org is disabled are not covered.
